section_summary.evidence_source: The section describes the measurement of 'Consideration of cosmetic surgery' using the 'Consider subscale of the ACSS', which contains five items assessing the likelihood that a respondent would consider having cosmetic surgery. All items were rated on a 7-point Likert-type scale (1 = Strongly disagree,7= Strongly agree) and an overall score was computed by taking the mean of the five items. Previous work has shown that this subscale has high internal consistency, good test– retest reliability, and good convergent and discriminant validity (Henderson-King & Henderson-King, 2005). In the present study, Cronbach's alpha for this subscale was .92.
